title: EFFINGHAM MAN ARRESTED
full_story:
An Effingham man was arrested over the weekend after police said he attacked another man with a machete and barricaded himself in a basement.

The incident happened in the area of 4th Street and Washington Avenue.  Officials with the Effingham Police Department said it was reported Sunday at about 5 pm, and officers arrived to find one person with minor injuries and a child located on the main floor of the home.  They were able to get the child out safely.

Effingham Police said that Officers were made aware that the suspect had retreated to the basement of the residence.  Officers were able to make verbal contact with the suspect, who was later identified as William R. Allen, 39, Effingham.  He refused multiple requests to come out of the basement.

The standoff lasted about two hours, during which additional law enforcement agencies arrived to assist.  Officers eventually obtained a search warrant to gain access to the home, but before it could be served, Allen agreed to comply with officers’ demands and surrendered without incident.

Allen was initially transported to St. Anthony’s Memorial Hospital for an evaluation before being booked into the Effingham County Jail.  He was charged with Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, a Class 3 felony, Domestic battery with previous convictions, a Class 4 felony, and Obstruction of a police officer, a Class A misdemeanor.

Allen appeared in court on Monday for arraignment and a detention hearing.  Effingham Police said Judge Bryan M. Kibler found probable cause to deny Allen pretrial release.

title: STATE FFA CONVENTION
full_story:
The Illinois State FFA Convention began this morning at the Bank of Springfield Center, in Springfield and a number of North Clay FFA Members are taking part.

Paige Pittman will play piano during the State FFA Degree Ceremony and Laila Smith will also take to the stage to perform during the 2 pm session tomorrow.

Bella Price was selected to play in the state band and Brianna Merrill and Evelyn Stone will be part of the state chorus and will be performing today during session 2, tomorrow during session 3 and 4 and again on Thursday in session 5.

Mila Zink from North Clay and Mikenzie Alvis from the Cisne FFA will be recognized as Top 10 Chapter Reporters.

Haven Cash will be recognized as an Illinois State winner in Agricultural Communication tomorrow during the Session 3.  Haven is also one of 10 candidates eligible for election to one of six Illinois FFA Major State Officer positions; president, vice president, reporter, secretary, treasurer or sentinel on Thursday.  Haven is currently serving as both the North Clay FFA chapter president and Section 23 FFA president.

The 98th annual Illinois FFA State Convention runs through Thursday.

title: FRANK & BRIGHT FLAG EXCHANGE
full_story:
Frank & Bright Funeral Home will once again host its annual Flag Exchange on Friday, June 12th from 8 am until 6 pm at the funeral home.  This is a one-day-only event.

You are invited to bring in a well-served US flag and exchange it for a new 3′ x 5′ outdoor American flag, made in the U.S.A.  One complimentary flag will be offered per household.  Additional flags may be purchased at a modest cost.

Ryan Muskopf, Daniel Fopay, Robert Bruns, and the staff of Frank & Bright Funeral Home are hosting the Flag Exchange as a way to honor current and former members of the armed forces, law enforcement, and all of our first responders.

title: WILHOUR FISHING DERBY
full_story:
State Representative Blaine Wilhour will host his 4th Annual Kids Fishing Derby on Saturday, at Willow Pond, located next to the visitor center at Carlyle Lake at 801 Laker Road in Carlyle.

The event is open to children ages 4 to 15 and is being held in partnership with the Illinois Department of Natural Resources and the US Army Corps of Engineers.

The fishing derby begins at 9:00 am with presentations on water safety and instruction on how to bait a hook, cast a line, and reel in a fish.  Children must be accompanied by an adult.

“This event is a great opportunity for kids to learn how to fish for the first time or simply enjoy the outdoors at one of Illinois’ premier fishing destinations,” said Wilhour.  “We’ll once again be awarding prizes for the biggest fish caught and the most fish caught during the derby.”

For questions, please contact the district office at 618-665-4109 or online at RepWilhour.com.  The phone number at the Carlyle Lake visitor Center is 618-594-5253.

title: WAYNE COUNTY MOST WANTED

The six suspects on the “Most Wanted” list and their charges are:

Margaret M. VanMater, 47, of Cisne is wanted for failure to appear in court on charges of possession of a controlled substance, driving under the influence of an intoxicating compound and identity theft.

Mikkel J. Pierce, 21, of Albion is wanted for violation of a stayed sentence on an original conviction of burglary and possession of methamphetamine.

title: PLUMMER TOWN HALLS
full_story:
State Senator Jason Plummer is set to host two End of Session Town Hall events Monday, to provide residents with an update on recent legislative activity from the 2026 spring session.  The meetings will take place in Olney and in Salem.

The events are free and open to the public.  Residents are encouraged to attend to learn more about actions taken during the spring session, ask questions, and share feedback on issues important to their communities.

In Olney the meeting will be held from 5 to 6 pm at the Olney Public Library.  In Salem the meeting will be held from 7 to 8 pm at the Salem Education Center.  Residents are encouraged to attend, learn more about the spring legislative session, and ask questions about state government.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
Statewide, the USDA says 96% of the corn crop is planted, up 5% from last week, with 88% emerged, and 67% rated good to excellent, while 93% of soybeans are planted, up 4% from last week, with 84% emerged and 64% in good to excellent condition.  The Illinois winter wheat crop is rated 73% in good to excellent condition with 4% harvested.

There were 6 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending June 7th.  Statewide, the average temperature was 72.7 degrees, 3.4 degrees above average.  Statewide precipitation averaged .52 of an inch, .56 of an inch below normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 8% very short, 21% short, 63% adequate, and 8% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 5% very short, 29% short, 59% adequate, and 7% surplus.

Corn planted reached 96%, compared to the 5-year average of 95%.  Corn emerged reached 88%, compared to the 5-year average of 90%.  Corn condition was rated 1% very poor, 4% poor, 28% fair, 55% good, and 12% excellent.

Soybeans planted reached 93%, compared to the 5-year average of 91%.  Soybeans emerged reached 84%, compared to the 5-year average of 80%.  Soybeans condition was rated 1% very poor, 4% poor, 31% fair, 52% good, and 12% excellent.

Winter wheat headed reached 95%, compared to the 5-year average of 97%.  Winter wheat condition was rated 1% very poor, 6% poor, 20% fair, 61% good, and 12% excellent.  Winter wheat harvest has started with 4% of the crop reportedly harvested, compared to the 5 year average of 1%.

title: IDOT URGING SAFETY
full_story:
Construction season is underway across the state, and leaders from the Illinois Department of Transportation are encouraging driver safety as more highways are covered in orange barrels.

Paul Wappel, Spokesman for IDOT, says drivers need to slow down and pay attention.

Each year, IDOT reports nearly 6,200 accidents in work zones across the state, resulting in more than 1,000 injuries.
